Context/Background:
Circular RNA (circRNA) is a class of noncoding RNA with regulatory potentials. Here, we identified circRMST as an exceptionally abundant circRNA predominantly expressed in neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC) and small cell lung cancer (SCLC), with strong conservation between humans and mice.

To explore the functional role of circRMST, we designed two shRNAs targeting the backspliced junction (BSJ), achieving 70%–93% knockdown efficiency. In 3D Matrigel-embedded cultures, circRMST knockdown significantly impaired cell growth across three NEPC and four SCLC-A models. Additionally, cell cycle analysis in SHP77 cells revealed cell-cycle arrest. In vivo, SHP77 xenografts in NSG immunodeficient mice exhibited markedly reduced tumor growth upon circRMST depletion.
Prompt:
To investigate transcriptional changes following circRMST knockdown, we performed RNA-seq in SHP77 cells and identified hundreds of differentially expressed genes.

What are the most relevant pathways in a GSEA results with the differential gene list?  Nominate a target most relevant for neuroendocrine prostate cancer.

Introduction/Context  
CircRMST is a circular RNA highly expressed in neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC) and small-cell lung cancer (SCLC), regulated by back‐splicing of RMST. Two independent shRNAs targeting the circRMST back‐spliced junction achieved 70–93% knockdown in SHP77 NEPC cells, leading to hundreds of significant DE genes by RNA-seq. Cell‐cycle arrest was observed in 3D Matrigel cultures, and circRMST depletion impaired in vivo SHP77 xenograft growth. The exact number of replicates is not specified.

Analysis  
Across KEGG and GO libraries, anabolic and metabolic programs (TCA cycle, glutathione/glucose metabolism, amino-acid starvation response, mTORC1 signaling) are strongly upregulated, whereas many neuropeptide/GPCR‐mediated signaling pathways (neuroactive ligand–receptor interaction; GPCR ligand binding; Hedgehog signaling) are suppressed. High up/down ratios in Reactome (4.3) and Hallmarks (11.0) reflect concerted induction of growth‐promoting and stress‐response modules alongside broad receptor downregulation. Enrichment of “Mitotic Spindle” and “E2F Targets” underscores cell‐cycle disruption, consistent with the observed arrest.

Comparisons & Confidence  
The concordance of metabolic and cell‐cycle upregulation with GPCR suppression in a neuroendocrine background highlights a shift from receptor‐driven growth to metabolic reprogramming. GPCR hits (P2RY2, ADORA1) are likely direct circRMST targets given the strong negative NES, while mTOR‐axis induction (MTOR, SESN3) represents a compensatory stress response. Single‐modality motifs (e.g., adipogenesis) are lower confidence.

Implications  
mTOR emerges as a high‐value therapeutic target in circRMST‐driven NEPC. Its dual role in amino‐acid sensing and cell‐cycle regulation suggests rapalogs or next‐generation mTORC1 inhibitors may synergize with circRNA modulation.

Next Steps & Clarifications  
1. Validate mTOR pathway activation by phospho‐S6K/IHC in circRMST‐knockdown SHP77 xenografts.  
2. Test mTORC1 inhibitors (e.g., everolimus) in combination with circRMST ASOs for synergy.  
3. Confirm suppression of key GPCRs (P2RY2, ADORA1) at protein level and assess downstream cAMP/PKA signaling.  
4. Verify presence or absence of Hedgehog pathway modulation (Gli2, SMO) in this model (not strongly observed by GSEA).
